proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved exact covariance-fibre enumeration with at most k! numerical SEMs and O(k!p^3) exact-real work, plus joint-intervention mean recovery by mapping that fibre. The math panel passed, but D0.5.G graded the delivered package subfield below the field floor and found no bounded tier lift. General fixed-profile maxima, finite-sample theory, and a complete priority comparison remain open; the separate decision-panel positioning findings were not repaired.
tldr: For a centered linear acyclic SEM with mutually independent finite-variance errors and a known partition into equal-variance blocks, one positive-definite covariance determines an exact finite numerical fibre: block activation recovers every compatible coefficient matrix and block-variance vector, including exceptional intersections, with at most \(k!\) outputs and deterministic \(O(k!p^3)\) exact-real work. Comparing all joint-intervention mean coefficient vectors over that fibre gives an if-and-only-if identification criterion and explicit countermodels on failure. Gaussian errors are the principal published specialization, not a requirement of the proof. With two blocks, marginal variance minima and \(\det(\Sigma)\) reduce the fibre to at most two models independently of \(p\).
gap: Existing partial-homoscedasticity theory characterizes equality of global DAG models or generic identification of one scalar effect. It does not describe all numerical mechanisms at a fixed covariance where unequal models intersect.
fill: Block activation adapts ancestral conditional-variance peeling so branching occurs only when a new variance block is first calibrated. Soundness, completeness, a \(k!\) bound, a two-block classification, and an exact joint-effect decision theorem form the paper's core.
